headline: Generative and physics-based models resolve RNA and protein conformational ensembles
label: Conformational Ensemble Modeling
summary: Physics-based and generative methods now benchmark conformational landscapes against smFRET, NMR and MD reference data.
synthesis: The common thread is computational recovery of conformational ensembles for RNA and proteins, with outputs judged against experimental or simulation references. Integrative modeling fuses smFRET with all-atom MD and in silico FRET prediction to resolve Mg2+-dependent bound and unbound RNA tertiary-contact mixtures. MERGE-RNA fits secondary-structure ensembles to DMS probing data using a maximum-entropy formulation, while a multiscale hairpin framework couples adaptive MD with Markov state models and latent generative flows. On the protein side, TopoFlow conditions flow matching on MSA and VAE latents, ENM-BD applies coarse-grained Brownian dynamics across more than 8,500 proteins benchmarked against MD and NMR, and a Gaussia luciferase study compares AlphaFold, BioEmu and extended MD with PT-WTE sampling. AlloPool extracts allosteric networks from MD using a GNN. What is new is the pairing of generative or coarse-grained sampling with experimental observables such as smFRET and DMS data.
